Benched Budew came into play THIS turn and its Itchy Pollen costs NOTHING -- it is the item-lock disruptor. decision.why:
HELD OUT by user ruling 2026-07-28 during #177's grill: this frame belongs to the gusting work, #189 (Phase 1e-iv, repoint gust-target onto the shared marginal). The agent's chosen option IS a gust Supporter and the only rule that fired on it is `stall-gust-over-dev-when-starved` at 92.0, so whether Boss's Orders is worth its slot here is exactly the gust marginal #189 repoints. #177 changes KO affordability and touches none of it.

MEASURED, so #189 does not have to re-derive it. The correct option NEVER MOVED: Retreat scores 62.50 both at the pinned baseline (81eac82) and on current main. What flipped the verdict is three SIBLINGS climbing by exactly +2.70 each -- both Ultra Balls and Boss's Orders went 62.05 -> 64.75, stepping over Retreat and taking correct_rank 1 -> 4, top_tie 1 -> 3. `End` did not move (60.025), so the shift is specific to the play-a-card continuations, not to Dreepy staying Active. A uniform delta across exactly those three is a systematic positional shift in the rollout's own continuation, not noise.

The margin it lost was 0.45 points on a ~62-point scale (0.7%) -- a unique top by a hair. The human's own rationale agrees it is near-indifferent ('doesnt really make a difference'), which is the same shape as 85164605|1|decision|41, already held out to #145 as 'a NEAR-INDIFFERENT turn whose residual is a readiness-currency question'. If #189 concludes the gust marginal is not what moved here, #145 (`_readiness` and the currency audit) is the other candidate owner.

DETERMINISTIC, not #160's RNG: three independent process runs returned [64.75, 64.75, 64.75, 62.5, 60.025] identically, rank 4, tie 3. So it is attributable to a change merged between the baseline pin (151f441) and 9a0a8ec -- the candidates touching this surface are #175's probability weighting and #178's rollout fixes, plus the famine premise swap (f0266e3, cb3933e, 9092c27, 0c13730) that `stall-gust-over-dev-when-starved` reads.

ADDENDUM 2026-07-28 (#186 follow-up, measured on main @ 7d2a656 — OWNER DELIBERATELY LEFT AT #189; this is evidence for the owner call, not a re-ruling of it). Two facts the ruling above could not have had:

(1) THE PREMISE IS NOW STALE. 'The agent's chosen option IS a gust Supporter' describes the RECORDED trace (build 32530b9, which chose [2] Boss's Orders). Re-running the SHIPPED pilot on this obs today returns chosen=[0] — Ultra Ball. The agent no longer plays the gust here, so 'whether Boss's Orders is worth its slot' is no longer the live question on this frame. What remains is that it will not RETREAT.

(2) THE MANEUVER RUNG EXISTS AND IS GATED OFF. The human's correct line (retreat Dreepy into Budew, Ultra Ball a Drakloak, evolve, Recon Directive, then Itchy Pollen) is exactly `pilot._can_lock_line_with_disruptor` ('retreat the pivot/line-preevo into Budew -> promote -> Itchy Pollen', gated turn<=2; this is turn 2). `disruptor_lock_maneuver` is armed ON, and the rung still returns False here — blocked by its own f21 guard: 'a wincon Line body is already being energized -> develop it, don't retreat for the lock'. Dreepy (119) carries [2]. `_can_wall_line_with_disruptor` also declines (Duraludon has 0 Energy, so it cannot damage us yet). So agent and human disagree here BY DESIGN, on a doctrine boundary, not by an accident.

OWNER CANDIDATES, unresolved. The ruling above names #145 as the fallback if the gust marginal is not what moved. Fact (2) suggests a third: by ADR-0070 amendment J's test — is the action individually valuable the moment it becomes legal? — the retreat is NOT (it discards our only Energy, which cannot be replaced this turn since energyAttached is already true, and promotes a 30 HP body). It pays only as a dependent chain, which is the definition of a Maneuver => #165 (the Turn Planner). Re-ruling or scoping the f21 boundary is the other shape the fix could take. Left for the user to rule between #189 / #145 / #165.

RESOLVED 2026-07-29 (user ruling). The f21 energized-line guard in `_can_lock_line_with_disruptor` is DELETED: 'too strict — in this case we are severely behind and must protect our dreepy while slowing down our opponent', and such decisions are value equation and turn planner candidates rather than a boolean rung guard. The guard's cited `f21` (`dragapult_dont_feed_draw_engine_f21`) is an ATTACH frame — put the off-type {D} into Dreepy rather than the Dunsparce draw engine — and never spoke to retreating, so it had generalised a WHERE-to-attach ruling into a veto on a different decision.

MEASURED after the deletion: this frame's DECIDER now returns [3] Retreat, matching the human. Blast radius is exactly ONE frame across all 331 replayable corrections — this one — with zero regressions. The Discrimination Gate is PASS with ZERO verdict flips against the 38ca76f baseline, so the leaf did not move at all; what changed is which rung wins, not how the leaf ranks. Full strategy+agents suites green (1737 passed).

WHAT REMAINS, and its owner. The decider-level defect is fixed, but the LEAF still mis-ranks this frame — options [0][1][2] sit at 64.75 over Retreat's 62.50, which is why the leaf verdict stays MISS and is now baked into the baseline. That residual is the value-equation / turn-planner question the user named: what a protection-plus-disruption turn is worth when we are behind, composed across a multi-step turn. Owners #145 (currency/readiness) and #165 (the Turn Planner Maneuver). The #189 gust reading is retired — the agent no longer plays the gust on this frame.

THIRD DEFECT, recorded 2026-07-29 (user, on the same frame) — THE ATTACH COLOUR, and it is NOT this frame's to fix. The turn already spent its attach before this select (`energyAttached: true`), putting Basic {R} on the Dreepy. If the plan is to retreat that Dreepy the same turn to promote Budew, the retreat cost DISCARDS that Energy (rules.md L89), so the attach should have been the Basic {D} sitting in hand.

VERIFIED AT SOURCE why {D} is the right card to burn and {R} is not. Typed demand across this deck: Dreepy Bite {R}{P}, Drakloak Dragon Headbutt {R}{P}, Dragapult ex Phantom Dive {R}{P}, Munkidori Mind Bend {P}(dot). {D} appears in NO typed cost — it can only ever pay a colourless slot (Jet Headbutt (dot), Mind Bend's (dot)), so it is the deck's only fungible Energy. Supply in the 60 on this board: {R} x3 (2 deck + 1 attached), {P} x3 (2 deck + 1 prized), {D} x2 (1 deck + 1 hand). So paying the retreat with {R} spends a THIRD of the hard-typed supply the win condition needs, to buy something a {D} would have bought for free.

OWNER: #165, with the colour choice falling out of the existing attach marginal once the plan exists. By ADR-0070 amendment J's test the attach of {D} onto Dreepy is individually worthless ({D} pays neither {P} nor {R}{P}) and pays only as step 1 of attach -> retreat -> promote -> lock: a Maneuver. But NO new heuristic is needed and nothing should encode 'prefer Darkness' — once the Turn Planner commits 'this body retreats this turn', Energy attached to it is SPENT, not banked, so its build value is 0 and the attach equation already prefers the most fungible card on its own. #165 supplies the plan; the equation prices the colour given the plan (#136: #165 'composes the equations across a turn rather than replacing any of them').

`feed-the-line-for-disruptor-lock` already half-encodes this — 'the energy is DELIBERATELY spent to pay the enabling retreat, so its worth is the LOCK, not the build' — but it only says WHERE to attach (the Active), never WHICH card. NOTE the attach happened at an EARLIER, probably untagged frame in this turn, so this defect is unreachable from frame 13 in principle — which is itself the argument that it is turn-level rather than per-frame.

OWNER MOVED #189 -> #165 (user ruling, 2026-07-29): 'we already ruled that f21 is a turn planner issue, thus we dont care about now. not our business.' The frame stays HELD OUT — reported, never gating — until #165 owns it.

The #189 gust reading is retired: the agent no longer plays Boss's Orders here (it returns [0] Ultra Ball), so 'is the gust worth its slot' is not the live defect. What remains is a Maneuver in two parts, both #165's: it will not RETREAT into the lock, and the attach that would fund the retreat spends a wincon-typed {R} where the fungible {D} belongs.

The f21 energized-line guard deletion that would have fixed the retreat here was REVERTED — it failed the ADR-0072 mid-build paired A/B (delta -4.75%, CI [-8.22%, -1.28%], 0 crashes / 2400 games, all six directed matchups negative). The doctrine that the guard is too strict still stands; a bare deletion is simply not the way to act on it, because the same gate also feeds the w55 `feed-the-line-for-disruptor-lock` ATTACH rung and ungating that diverts Energy away from the build on boards the corpus never samples. So this frame is expected to MISS until #165 lands — that expectation is the hold-out, and it is why the frame must not gate.
